newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lonrho falls on end of JCI talks.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho falls on end of JCI talks.

text.p: Lonrho South Africa shed 4.5 percent shortly after news British hotels-to-mining conglomerate Lonrho Plc had shut down merger talks with South African mining house JCI Ltd.
The share was last 35 cents weaker at 970 cents in a turnover of 250,900 shares. It fell as far as 960 cents on the news before recovering slightly.

Lonrho Plc said earlier in London that it had discontinued talks with JCI on a possible merger of the two groups. It gave no further details in teh statement. The two companies said last month they were in preliminary discussions.
"It (Lonrho) went down quite substantially straight after the announcement, but I don't know why they've broken off the talks. It doesn't say," said James Scott of Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
"It (the deal) was seen as facilitating a number of things for Lonrho and Anglo as well. Any terminating of talks these days is seen as negative," he said.

JCI on Monday said it had no immediate comment on the end of the talks. On Friday the South African mining house also declined to comment on a Financial Times report quoting advisers close to JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo saying he was close to abandoning talks with Lonrho on the merger.
A merger between Lonrho and JCI -- South Africa's first black-controlled mining house -- could create a mining company with a market capitalisation of over $3 billion.
Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, pressured by the European Commission, agreed in April to cut its 27 percent stake in Lonrho to under 10 percent.

Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson told analysts during a briefing last week that Lonrho had mooted the idea of swapping its 33.6 percent stake in Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd for Anglo's disputed Lonrho stake.
Dealers said that Lonrho sahres could fall further.
"The possibility is there but there don't seem to be that many bids around," a dealer said.
Another dealer said he expected JCI to fall slightly. It was steady at 35.50 rand a share.
